description: One cup of powdered sugar weighs 113 grams, unsifted and levelled. Convert powdered sugar between cups and grams, with the table and worked examples.

steps: Multiply by the weight of one cup: 2 × 113 g.
examples.title: 2 cups of powdered sugar to grams

steps: Divide by the weight of one cup: 200 ÷ 113.
examples.title: 200 g of powdered sugar to cups

faqs.answer: 113 grams, when the cup is unsifted, spooned and levelled. That is the figure on King Arthur Baking's ingredient weight chart for confectioners' sugar.
faqs.question: How many grams are in a cup of powdered sugar?

faqs.answer: Yes. Sifting fluffs the sugar up, so a sifted cup holds less and weighs less than 113 grams. King Arthur does not list a sifted weight. If a recipe says '1 cup powdered sugar, sifted', measure first, then sift.
faqs.question: Does sifted powdered sugar weigh less than unsifted?

faqs.answer: 16 tablespoons, and each one weighs about 7 grams. A quarter cup is 4 tablespoons, about 28 grams.
faqs.question: How many tablespoons are in a cup of powdered sugar?

faqs.answer: About 4.4 cups. 500 ÷ 113 = 4.42 cups, which is 4 cups plus about 7 tablespoons.
faqs.question: How many cups is 500 g of powdered sugar?

faqs.answer: Yes. They are two names for the same thing: granulated sugar ground to a fine powder, with a little cornstarch mixed in to stop it clumping. Use either name on the bag. The weight per cup is the same.
faqs.question: Is powdered sugar the same as confectioners' sugar?

felicityNote: I sift powdered sugar straight into the bowl now, over the butter, and let the lumps stay behind in the sieve. Smooth icing, every time.

parts.meaning: The volume in the recipe, measured unsifted, spooned and levelled.
The grams in one cup of unsifted powdered sugar, from King Arthur Baking's chart.
The weight on the scale. The number that does not change with how you fill the cup.

howToSteps.name: Break up the lumps
howToSteps.text: Press the lumps out of the sugar with a fork, or give the bag a shake, before you measure. Hard lumps leave air pockets in the cup and the weight comes out wrong.

howToSteps.name: Spoon it into the cup
howToSteps.text: Spoon the sugar into the measuring cup until it heaps over the top. Do not scoop with the cup itself. Scooping packs the fine powder down.

howToSteps.name: Level it off
howToSteps.text: Sweep the flat edge of a knife across the rim of the cup, back into the bag. The cup is now level and holds one cup, 113 grams.

howToSteps.name: Sift if the recipe needs it
howToSteps.text: For icing or dusting, sift the sugar after measuring. Sifting breaks up the last lumps and makes the icing smooth. Measure first, then sift. A sifted cup weighs less than an unsifted one.

name: Powdered Sugar
sourceNote: King Arthur Baking lists confectioners' sugar, unsifted, at 113 g per cup (4 oz).
title: Powdered Sugar Cups to Grams Converter
tutorial: Powdered sugar is strange stuff to measure. It is ground so fine that it packs down in the bag and clumps into hard little lumps. A cup can hold more or less of it depending on how it was filled, which is why icing sometimes comes out stiff and sometimes too soft.

The number on this page comes from King Arthur Baking's ingredient weight chart: one cup of powdered sugar, unsifted, spooned and levelled, weighs 113 grams. Unsifted matters. Sifting fluffs the sugar up and a sifted cup weighs less. This converter uses the unsifted weight, because that is how most recipes mean it when they say '1 cup powdered sugar'.

Measure it like flour: spoon it into the cup until it heaps over the top, then sweep a knife across the rim. Do not scoop straight from the bag. Scooping packs the fine powder down and you end up with more sugar than the recipe wants. If you are making icing, sift the sugar after measuring. Lumps are the enemy of smooth frosting.

Use the converter in either direction. A recipe in cups becomes grams when you want the accuracy of the scale. A recipe in grams becomes cups when the scale is in a drawer somewhere and you are already halfway through mixing. One anchor to remember: half a cup is about 57 grams, two cups is 226 grams. Most icing recipes land on those numbers.

One thing worth knowing: powdered sugar and confectioners' sugar are the same thing, and both contain a little cornstarch to stop clumping. That is why it never quite behaves like granulated sugar in a recipe. Do not swap them cup for cup. The two weigh very different amounts per cup.
